questions.question: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) is a scheme launched by the Hon'ble Prime Minister of India on April 8, 2015 for providing ______ to the non - corporate enterprises.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**loan.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **PMMY **aims to provide loans up to **Rs. 10** lakhs to** non-corporate small business units.**
 
• PMMY has been launched under the aegis of the **Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency **(MUDRA) which is a subsidiary of Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI).
 
• The objective of PMMY is to **promote entrepreneurship** and facilitate the growth of small businesses in the country by providing easy access to credit.
 
• The scheme offers three types of loans: **Shishu** (up to Rs. 50,000), **Kishore** (Rs. 50,001 to Rs. 5 lakhs) and **Tarun** (Rs. 5,00,001 to Rs. 10 lakhs).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Skill training** is provided under other schemes such as **Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana.**

 
 
• **​Encouraging aptitude** towards employable skills and boosting working efficiency of potential and current daily wage earners are the goals of the PMKVY scheme.
 
• The average prize amount per individual has remained at **₹8,000.**
 
 
 
• **House subsidy** is provided under schemes such as **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana.**
 
 
• **​**It is divided into two parts: the **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana** (Urban) (PMAY-U) for the impoverished in urban areas, and the** Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana **(Gramin) (PMAY-G and PMAY-R) for those in rural areas.
 
• The **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs **oversees the former, while the** Ministry of Rural Development** oversees the latter.
 
 

2f:T

questions.question: Charu Sija Mathur is a name that is synonymous with ______ dance.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manipuri.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Manipuri dance **is commonly associated with **Charu Sija Mathur.**

 
 
• Charu Sija Mathur hails from a well-known, culturally conscious family in **Delhi.**
 
 
 
• Manipuri is a classical dance form that originated in the northeastern state of **Manipur, **India.
 
 
• It is characterized by** graceful movements, intricate footwork,** and the use of traditional Manipuri costumes and musical instruments.
 
• The dance form is deeply rooted in the **culture and mythology** of Manipur, and often depicts stories from **Hindu mythology** and the lives of the people of Manipur.
 
• Manipuri dance is known for its **fluidity and softness**, and is often performed in a **circular pattern**, with the dancers moving in and out of the circle.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chhau** is a traditional dance form from **eastern India,** primarily performed in the states of **Jharkhand, West Bengal, and Odisha**.

 
 
• It is known for its **martial arts**-inspired movements and use of** masks.**
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi** is a classical dance form from the southern state of **Andhra Pradesh, **India.
 
 
• It is characterized by **fast footwork, intricate hand gestures**, and expressive facial expressions.
 
 
 
• **Odissi** is a classical dance form from the eastern state of **Odisha, India**.
 
 
• It is known for its **fluid movements, graceful poses**, and use of hand gestures and facial expressions.

questions.question: Which of the following Hindu goddesses is worshipped during the festival of Gangaur?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parvati.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gangaur **is a festival celebrated in **Rajasthan, Haryana, **and parts of **Gujarat **and **Madhya Pradesh.**
 
• It is a celebration of the **harvest season **and the onset of spring.
 
• During Gangaur, married women worship the goddess **Parvati,** who symbolizes **marital bliss and fertility.**
 
• The festival lasts for **18 days** and culminates with a grand procession of the idol of Parvati and her consort **Shiva.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saraswati **is the goddess of **knowledge, music, arts, and science**.

 
 
• She is worshipped during the festival of **Saraswati Puja.**
 
 
 
• **Kali** is the goddess of **time, change, and destruction**.
 
 
• She is worshipped during the festival of** Kali Puja.**
 
 
 
• **Lakshmi **is the goddess of **wealth, prosperity, and fortune.**
 
 
• She is worshipped during the festival of **Diwali.**

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India sets out the different Fundamental Duties for Indian citizens?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 51A.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 51A** sets out the different **Fundamental Duties** for Indian citizens.
 
• The moral duty of all people to support the growth of **patriotism and the preservation** of India's unity is referred to as the Fundamental Duties.

 
• The Indian Constitution's **Part IVA** governs Fundamental Duties.
 
• There are currently **eleven** fundamental duties.
 
• The Constitution was amended by the **42nd and 86th Constitutional Amendment Acts**, adding basic duties.
 
• The Constitution requires citizens to carry out their duties in an **ethical manner.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Moral and civic duties **are the two categories into which fundamental duties fall.

 
 
• Moral duty includes upholding the lofty goals of the **freedom movement.**
 
• **Respecting** the Constitution, the flag, and the national anthem is a civic duty.
 
 
 
• Unlike several other Fundamental Rights, the Fundamental Duties are **exclusive to Indian nationals **and do not apply to foreigners.
 
• Similar to the Directive Principles of State Policy, they are likewise **nonjusticiable.**
 
• There is** no legal repercussion** for their transgression.

questions.question: Article 76 of the Indian Constitution deals with ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Attorney - General for India.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 76** of the Indian Constitution deals with the appointment, duties, qualifications, and powers of the **Attorney-General for India.**
 
• The Attorney-General for India is the** highest law officer** of the country and acts as the** legal advisor **to the Government of India.
 
• The Attorney-General is appointed by the **President of India** and holds office during the pleasure of the President.
 
• The Attorney-General has the** right to speak** and take part in the proceedings of both the Houses of Parliament but is** not entitled to vote.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Council of Ministers **is a body of senior government officials who assist the **Prime Minister** in the administration of the country.

 
 
• **Article 74 **of the Indian Constitution deals with the Council of Ministers.
 
 
 
• The **Governor of India** is the constitutional head of a state in India and is appointed by the **President of India**.
 
 
• **Article 153** of the Indian Constitution deals with the Governor.
 
 
 
• The **Home Minister** is a senior cabinet minister in the Government of India and is responsible for** maintaining law and order** in the country.
 
 
• **Article 352 **of the Indian Constitution deals with emergency powers of the Home Minister.

questions.question: Who is serving as the 34th Foreign Secretary of India from 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vinay Mohan Kwatra.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vinay Mohan Kwatra** is serving as the** 34th Foreign Secretary of India** from **2022.**
 
• Vinay Mohan Kwatra is a **1988-batch Indian Foreign Service officer** who has held several key positions in the **Ministry of External Affairs,** including as **India's Ambassador to France** and Monaco and **India's High Commissioner** to Sri Lanka.
 
• The **chief administrative officer** of the **Ministry of External Affairs** and **India's top diplomat** is the** Foreign Secretary.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subrahmanyam Jaishankar **was the **33rd Foreign Secretary of India** who served from **January 2015 to January 2018**.

 
 
• He is currently serving as **India's Minister of External Affairs.**
 
• **Vijay Keshav Gokhale** was the 31st Foreign Secretary of India who served from January 2018 to January 2020.

 He has previously served as India's Ambassador to China and as India's High Commissioner to Malaysia.
 
 
 
• **Harsh Vardhan Shringla** was the **33rd Foreign Secretary of India** who served from **January 2020 to January 2022.**
 
 
• He is currently serving as** India's Ambassador** to the United States.
 
 
 
• The role of the Foreign Secretary of India is to act as the administrative head of the **Ministry of External Affairs **and to advise the Prime Minister and other Ministers on matters of foreign policy.
 
 
• The Foreign Secretary also represents** India in international forums** and negotiates with foreign governments on behalf of the Indian government.

questions.question: Which of the following cities emerged as the second capital of the Kushanas during their empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mathura.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kushanas** were a **Central Asian dynasty** that ruled over a vast empire in **South Asia** from the **1st to the 3rd century** CE.
 
• The Kushanas had **two capitals**, the first being **Purushpur** (modern-day Peshawar in Pakistan) and the second being** Mathura** (in Uttar Pradesh, India).
 
• Mathura emerged as the** second capital **of the Kushanas during the reign of** Kanishka I** (127-150 CE), who is considered the **greatest** of the Kushana kings.
 
• Mathura was a strategically important city as it was located at the junction of **two major trade routes **and was also a major center of **Buddhism and Hinduism.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kannauj **was an important city in medieval India and served as the capital of several dynasties, including the **Gurjara-Pratiharas** and the **Rashtrakutas.**

 
 
• The classical name **Kanyakubja **has been distorted to become the name of the city. 
 
 
 
• **Pataliputra **was the capital of the **Mauryan and Gupta empires** and was also an important center of learning and culture.
 
 
• The city of Pataliputra was founded by **Udayin** at the meeting point of the **Son and Ganges rivers. **

questions.question: ______ are known as the powerhouses of the cell.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mitochondria.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mitochondria** is known as the **powerhouses of the cell.**
 
• Mitochondria are organelles found in **eukaryotic cells** that are responsible for producing energy in the form of **ATP.**
 
• They have their own** DNA** and can **replicate themselves,** which suggests that they may have evolved from independent bacteria that were engulfed by early eukaryotic cells.
 
• Mitochondria have a **unique structure **that allows them to carry out their **function efficiently.**
 
• They are composed of an outer and inner membrane, with the inner membrane folded into structures called **cristae.**
 
• Mitochondria are involved in a range of cellular processes beyond energy production, including **calcium signaling, apoptosis**, and the **synthesis of certain biomolecules.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lysosomes** are organelles that contain **digestive enzymes**.

 
 
• They are involved in **breaking down** cellular waste and foreign substances.
 
 
 
• **Ribosomes** are molecular machines that **synthesize proteins**.
 
 
• Some are located in the **cytoplasm** and others attached to the **endoplasmic reticulum.**
 
 
 
• The **nucleus** is the organelle that contains the** genetic material **of the cell and regulates **gene expression.**
 
 
• The **nuclear membrane, chromosomes, nucleoplasm,** and **nucleolus** make up the nucleus' structural components.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of direct tax?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Personal income tax.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **direct tax** is a tax that is paid directly to the** government** by the taxpayer.
 
• It is usually based on the** income or wealth** of the taxpayer.
 
• **Personal income tax **is a** direct tax** that is levied by the government on the income of individuals, including **salaries, wages, **and other forms of income.
 
• It is a **progressive tax**, which means that the **tax rate increases **as the income of the taxpayer increases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Custom duty** is a tax that is levied on goods that are** imported or exported** from a country.

 
 
• It is usually charged as a percentage of the value of the goods and is collected by** customs officials **at the border.
 
 
 
• **Excise tax** is a tax that is levied on goods that are produced **within a country**.
 
 
• It is usually charged as a percentage of the value of the goods and is collected by the government from the **manufacturers or producers** of the goods.
 
 
 
• **G.S.T. **or Goods and Services Tax is a tax that is levied on the **sale of goods and services**.
 
 
• It is charged as a percentage of the value of the goods or services and is collected by **businesses** that are registered for G.S.T.

questions.question: The dimensions of the basketball court is measured ______ from the inner edge of the boundary line.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 28 × 15 m.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **basketball court** is a **rectangular court** with a standard size of **28 meters** in length and **15 meters** in width.
 
• The measurements are taken from the **inner edge **of the boundary line, which marks the playing area of the court.
 
• The playing area, with **baskets at either end**, is the basketball court. 
 
• The rims of each basket on an indoor basketball court are typically **3.048 meters high** and are almost always made of **polished wood**, typically maple.
 
• Common paving materials like **concrete or asphalt **are used to create outdoor surfaces.
 
• **Glass basketball courts** may be used in international competitions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The main goal of **basketball**, a team sport, is to **shoot a basketball **through the opponent's hoop while keeping the other team from doing the same.
 
• **Two teams,** usually consisting of **five players** each, engage in this activity. 
 
• Unless it is made from behind the three-point line, in which case it is for three points, a** field goal** is worth** two.** 
 
• Following a foul, the player who was fouled or chosen to shoot a technical foul is awarded **one, two, or three one-point free throws**.
 
• The timed play then **ends. **
 
• The team with the** most points** at the end of regulation play wins; however, if the score is tied at the completion of regulation play,** overtime** must be played.

questions.question: Who was the president of the first session of Congress held in 1885?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee** was the **president** of the **first session of Congress** held in **1885.**
 
• He was a prominent **Indian barrister** and a member of the **Indian National Association.**
 
• The first session of the Indian National Congress held in **1885** was attended by** 72 delegates **from across India. 
 
• The main objective of the Congress was to promote **political and social reforms** and to work towards Indian independence from British rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian National Congress was founded in **1885 by Allan Octavian Hume**.

 
 
• He was a **retired British civil servant **and a political reformer who played a significant role in the Indian independence movement.
 
 
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji** was the first Indian to be elected to the **British Parliament**.
 
 
• He was a prominent figure in the Indian National Congress and a **strong advocate **for Indian independence.
 
 
 
• **Dinshaw Wacha** was a** lawyer and politician** who served as the president of the **Indian National Congress in 1901**.
 
 
• He was a supporter of the **Swadeshi movement** and played a key role in the Indian independence movement.

questions.question: Which country is the smallest neighbouring country of India area wise?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhutan.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhutan** is the **smallest neighbouring** country of India area wise.
 
• Bhutan has an area of **38,394 square kilometers.**
 
• Bhutan is located in the **eastern Himalayas** and is known for its stunning natural beauty.
 
• Bhutan is a **landlocked country** and shares borders with **India, China, and Nepal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nepal** is located in the Himalayas and shares a border with India to the **north**.

 
 
• It has an area of **147,181 **square kilometers.
 
 
 
• **Sri Lanka** is an island nation located in the **Indian Ocean**.
 
 
• It has an area of **65,610 **square kilometers and is separated from India by the** Palk Strait.**
 
 
 
• **Maldives** is an island nation located in the Indian Ocean and has an area of **300 square kilometers.**
 
 
• **​**It is located south of India and is** not** a contiguous neighbour.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of endogenic forces?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Building mountains.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Endogenic forces** are the forces that originate from **within the Earth's crust** and result in the formation of landforms.
 
• **Building mountains** is an example of endogenic forces as it involves **tectonic activity** where two tectonic plates collide, leading to the **uplift of the Earth's crust **and the formation of mountains.
 
• **Glaciers** are a result of **exogenic forces **(external forces) such as changes in climate and weather patterns.
 
• **Sea-waves** are a result of **exogenic forces **such as wind patterns, tides, and ocean currents.
 
• **Wind** is also result of an **exogenic force** that shapes the Earth's surface by eroding and depositing sediments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Himalayas, the Andes, and the Rockies** are examples of mountain ranges formed due to tectonic activity.
 
• **Glaciers** are large masses of ice that form in** high-altitude areas** where the temperature is **below freezing**.
 
 
• They are formed due to a combination of factors such as **temperature, precipitation, and topography.**
 
• Glaciers can shape the landscape by **eroding rocks, creating valleys,** and leaving behind moraines (piles of rocks and debris).
 
 
 
• **Sea-waves **are created due to a combination of factors such as** wind patterns, tides, and ocean currents.**
 
 
• They can shape the coastline by eroding rocks, creating** sea cliffs**, and** depositing sediments** to form beaches.
 
 
 
• **Wind** is a result of differences in **atmospheric pressure** that cause air to move from high-pressure areas to low-pressure areas.
 
 
• Wind can shape the Earth's surface by eroding rocks, creating sand dunes, and depositing sediments to form landforms such as **deltas**.

questions.question: Identify an element that does NOT belong to the third period.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bromine.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bromine** (Br) is a **halogen **and is located in the** fourth period**.
 
• The third period includes elements from** sodium (Na)** to** argon (Ar)**.
 
• **Silicon **(Si) and **phosphorus** (P) are both located in the third period.
 
• **Argon** (Ar) is a **noble gas **and is located in the third period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Potassium (K), Calcium (Ca), Scandium (Sc), Titanium (Ti), Vanadium (V), Chromium (Cr), Manganese (Mn), Iron (Fe), Cobalt (Co), Nickel (Ni), Copper (Cu), Zinc (Zn), Gallium (Ga), Germanium (Ge), Arsenic (As), Selenium (Se), Bromine (Br), and Krypton (Kr) are the **elements** associated with Period 4.
 
• There are a total of** eighteen elements** in the fourth period of the current periodic table.
 
• **Ten** d block elements, **six** p block elements, and** two** s block elements are among them.

questions.question: Major Dhyan Chand was born in which of the following city of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Allahabad.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Major Dhyan Chand** was a **legendary Indian hockey player** who was born on **August 29, 1905**, in** Allahabad, Uttar Pradesh.**
 
• He is widely regarded as one of the **greatest hockey players** of all time and his contribution to the sport is unmatched.
 
• Major Dhyan Chand's real name was **Dhyan Singh** and he was from a family of hockey players.
 
• His father,** Sameshwar Dutt Singh**, was a Subedar in the British Indian Army and played hockey for the army team.
 
• Major Dhyan Chand joined the army himself in **1922** and was soon selected for the Indian Army hockey team.
 
• He went on to represent India in** three Olympic Games** and won **gold medals** in all of them.
 
• He was also a part of the Indian team that won the **1936 Berlin Olympics**, where he scored three goals in the final against Germany.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Allahabad**, the birthplace of Major Dhyan Chand, is a city in **Uttar Pradesh** that is known for its rich history and cultural heritage.

 
 
• It is located at the confluence of the **Ganges, Yamuna, and Saraswati **rivers and is considered one of the** holiest cities** in India.
 
 
 
• **Aligarh** is a city in Uttar Pradesh that is known for its educational institutions, including the famous **Aligarh Muslim University.**
 
• **Lucknow** is the **capital city **of Uttar Pradesh and is known for its rich history, culture, and cuisine.
 
• **Dehradun** is the **capital** city of **Uttarakhand** and is known for its scenic beauty and proximity to the** Himalayas.**

questions.question: ______ is an international body that lends capital to the government of various countries.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**World Bank.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Bank** was established in **1944** and is headquartered in **Washington D.C.**
 
• It is one of the **largest sources of funding** for development projects in the world.
 
• The World Bank provides** loans and grants** to governments of developing countries for various projects, including** infrastructure, education, health, and agriculture**, among others.
 
• The World Bank has two main institutions- the **International Bank for Reconstruction and Development** (IBRD) and the **International Development Association **(IDA), which provide loans and grants to countries based on their** income levels** and** development needs.**
 
• The World Bank also provides **technical assistance and advisory services** to governments for policy reforms and institutional strengthening to promote sustainable development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **State Bank of India** is the largest commercial bank in India, which provides banking services to** individuals, businesses, and corporate **clients.

 
 
• It is headquartered in **Mumbai.**
 
• Its chairperson is **Dinesh Kumar Khara.**
 
 
 
• **Reserve Bank of India **is the central bank of India, which regulates the **monetary policy and currency** circulation in the country.
 
 
• It is headquartered in** Mumbai.**
 
• Its governor is **Shaktikanta Das.**
 
 
 
• **Central Bank of India **is a **public sector bank** in India, which provides various banking services to customers, including loans, deposits, and investment products.
 
 
• MD CEO of Central Bank of India is **Matam Venkata Rao.**
 
• It is headquartered in Mumbai.

questions.question: In order to provide basic healthcare to all, ______ and ______ need to be integrated in our basic health infrastructure.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**accessibility and affordability.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Accessibility and affordability** need to be integrated into our** basic health infrastructure** along with education and technology.
 
• Accessibility and affordability are critical factors in ensuring that basic healthcare is available to all, especially those in** low-income** and **marginalized communities.**
 
• **Education** is important to** increase awareness** about healthcare and **disease prevention**, and to train healthcare professionals.
 
• **Technology **can be used to improve healthcare delivery, such as** telemedicine **and **electronic health** records.
 
• **Communication** is also important to ensure that healthcare information is **disseminated **effectively and accurately.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Indian government** has entered into credit arrangements with foreign organizations to borrow up to **Rs 13,879 crore** for the purpose of strengthening its **health infrastructure.**
 
• Loan agreements have been signed in order to supplement **PM-ABHIM,** which was introduced in** October 2021** and will last until **FY 2025–2026.**
 
• One of the biggest national initiatives in India to improve the nation's healthcare system is the **Prime Minister's Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission.**
 
• Its objectives are to create** 11,024 urban Health and Wellness Centers** across the nation and support 17,788 rural Health and Wellness Centers in **ten "high focus" states.**

questions.question: Which of the following is a folk dance of Mizoram?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cheraw dance.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cheraw dance** is a traditional folk dance of** Mizoram,** a state in northeastern India.
 
• It is also known as **bamboo dance** as it involves dancers moving in and out of a set of bamboo poles being held by other dancers.
 
• The **ladies dancers** enter and exit the bamboo formations with **grace**, while the **men dancers** manipulate the bamboos to a **rhythmic beat.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 **Dhumal dance **is a folk dance of Jammu and Kashmir.

 
 
• 
 
 It is performed by the** men of the Wattal tribe on specific auspicious occasions.**
 
 
 
 
 
• **Chhau dance** is a tribal** martial dance **form.
 
 
• It originated in eastern India, primarily in the states of **Jharkhand, West Bengal, and Odisha.**
 
 
 
• **Koli dance** is a folk dance of **Maharashtra,** a state in western India.
 
 
• It is performed by the **Koli community** during their festivals and celebrations.

questions.question: Norman Borlaug, father of Green Revolution in the world, was awarded ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nobel peace prize.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Norman Borlaug** was a renowned **American agronomist and humanitarian **who is often referred to as the **father of the Green Revolution.**
 
• He is credited with developing **high-yielding, disease-resistant wheat **varieties that helped increase food production in many countries.
 
• Borlaug was awarded the **Nobel Peace Prize in 1970** in recognition of his contributions to world peace through increasing food supply, particularly in developing countries.
 
• He was the **first agricultural scientist** to receive this prestigious award.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Green Revolution** was a period of **intense technological innovation** in agriculture that began in the mid-20th century and resulted in increased **crop yields and food production** in many parts of the world.

 
 
• It involved the development and dissemination of **high-yielding crop varieties**, the use of **chemical fertilizers and pesticides**, and improved **irrigation and farming practices.**
 
 
 
• The **Nobel Peace Prize** is awarded annually to individuals or organizations that have made significant contributions to promoting **peace and resolving conflicts. **
 
 
• **​**It is one of the five Nobel Prizes established by the** will of Swedish industrialist Alfred Nobel.**
 
 
 
• **Olympic medal** is a prestigious award given to athletes who excel in their respective **sports** at the Olympic Games. 
 
• **Bharat Ratna** is the **highest civilian award** in India, given for exceptional service in any field.
 
 
• It has been awarded to several distinguished personalities, including **scientists, artists, and social activists.**
 
 
 
• **Gallantry award** is a military decoration awarded to members of the** armed forces** for acts of bravery in combat.
 
 
• It includes awards such as the **Victoria Cross, Medal of Honor, and Cross of Valour.**
